Re: Develop a serializer&deserializer for R objects in JVM <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-145>

The package HistogramTools is under Apache 2.0 license and enhances Rprotobuf. OpenCpu has the same license and suggests Rprotobuf. The authors of both are co-authors to Rprotobuf. Histogramtools imports Hmisc and stringr and they are both GPL-2. It also suggests two GPL-2 packages. Histogramtools is copyright by Google as so I suspect some lawyer looked into the matter. Package foreach is apache 2.0 licensed and depends on codetools which is GPL2. If you need more assurances, I can reach out to one of the authors and get his explicit blessing. The language R and package methods are also GPL-2 and already listed among SparkR dependencies. SparkR is absolutely non-functional without R or methods, but doesn't include or modify either.

messages.body_plain:
Chris

Thanks a lot for posting the data and the code -- I used this to do a bunch of debugging and profiling today (but this was on a cluster with more memory). I've opened a PR with some fixes I made at https://github.com/amplab-extras/SparkR-pkg/pull/147

1. The cache on textFile works a little differently in SparkR vs. PySpark. In SparkR we cache JavaRDD encoded as strings, while Python encodes it in Python. The reason this is important is that Strings in Java take 2 bytes per character vs 1 byte in most other languages. So one workaround in your case is to cache an R encoded RDD by explicitly calling `lapply`. i.e. You can do "lines <- cache(lapply(textFile(sc, <filepath>), identity))" -- This halves the cached dataset size from what I observed (i.e. each partition is down from 1G to 500 MB)

2. I also found that in this case calling `strsplit` is slow and you probably don't want to do that every time. So another optimization could be to do `strsplit` before cache.

3. Finally we've recently merged a PR that removes the dependency on rJava. So you can skip that step during the installation process. I'll update the SparkR wiki soon.

Shivaram

messages.subject: [JIRA] (SPARKR-145) Develop a serializer&deserializer for R objects in JVM
messages.subject_clean: [JIRA] (SPARKR-145) Develop a serializer&deserializer for R objects in JVM
messages.body_plain:
Shivaram Venkataraman <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=shivaram> commented on  SPARKR-145 <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-145>

Re: Develop a serializer&deserializer for R objects in JVM <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-145>

Thanks Antonio Piccolboni <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=piccolbo> for the pointers to other packages. I think there is a technical question here and a licensing question and we need to look at them separately
The first is the technical question what is the most efficient serialization format for SparkR's requirements. As I said before, for the control path using hand-wrapped serialization is fast enough (our RPCs to the SparkRBackend take ~1 millisecond or so right now). For the data path we have been using R's native serialization partly because it is general and partly because it is the first thing we got working. We haven't had the chance to try out other techniques or do a thorough performance comparison and we welcome any efforts in this direction. There are some efforts in the community like the upcoming Spark Summit talk [1] on using Renjin and keeping everything in the JVM which are very promising.
On the licensing side thanks for the pointers to packages like Histogramtools, foreach. Given that the way the project is growing, we are hopeful of merging SparkR with the Apache Spark project at some point. In that case, the ASF legal team might also be able to provide more guidance on how to interpret licenses for R package dependencies. That said I'd like to keep this JIRA for discussing the technical aspects of serialization, deserialization first and discuss the licensing issue when we have a particular PR up for consideration.

[1] http://spark-summit.org/east/2015/talk/functionality-and-performance-improvement-of-sparkr-and-its-application

Martin Tapp <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=doctapp> commented on  SPARKR-184 <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-184>

Re: Support JdbcRDD <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-184>

Should be fairly easy as you can use RJDBC with code like this to read:

library(RJDBC)
SQLRead <- function(s)
{ drv <- JDBC("com.microsoft.sqlserver.jdbc.SQLServerDriver", classPath="/mypath/sqljdbc4.jar") c <- dbConnect(drv,paste("jdbc:sqlserver://myhost", "\\myserver:1234;databaseName=mydb;", "user=myuser;password=mypassword;")) r <- dbGetQuery(c, s) dbDisconnect(c) r }

Therefore, you could wrap the drv part using a function and require a connection string. Or wrap even the dbConnect in another function with a matching dbDisconnect. I think you can stick to supporting the same JdbcRDD constructor.

When I call lapplyPartition on it with a function that prints its arguments in stderr, the function gets called three times, the first two with the expected arguments and the third with an empty list as argument. I was wondering if that's a bug or if there are conditions under which that's possible. I apologize I don't have a simple test case ready yet. Alter parallelize to convert data frames to lists <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-195>
Issue Type:    Improvement
Assignee:   Unassigned
Created:   04/Feb/15 9:39 AM
Priority:    Minor

Re: lapplyPartition passes empty list to function <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-194>

I don't have time to try any harder to repro this without plyrmr. For the record this is the example

library(plyrmr)
plyrmr.options(backend = "spark")
df1 = mtcars[1:4,]
df2 = mtcars[3:6,]
w = as.data.frame(gapply(merge(input(df1), input(df2)), identity))

the gapply is implemented with a lapplyPartition in most cases. The merge with a join. as.data.frame with a collect. The join has an arbitrary argument of 4 partitions. If I turn that down to 2L, the problem disappears. I will check in a version with a workaround in place but a debugging statement will leave a record in stderr whenever the workaround kicks in, so that we can track it.

Shivaram Venkataraman <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=shivaram> commented on  SPARKR-196 <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-196>

Re: wrong scope in slave process <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-196>

Thanks Antonio Piccolboni <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=piccolbo> for reporting this bug. It took a while to track this down and it turns out the bug is actually in the way we serialize dependencies. When we try to capture the value for `t` the `base` environment is picked up before `GlobalEnv` – I am not sure why the `base` package env comes up before `GlobalEnv` in the parent traversal order and I don't know of a good work-around yet.

cc hao <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=hlin> – It might be interesting to see if this error goes away in the new dependency capture proposed in https://github.com/amplab-extras/SparkR-pkg/pull/158

SparkR <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR> /  <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-197> SPARKR-197 <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-197>
Add a model.matrix like capability to DataFrames (modelDataFrame) <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-197>
Issue Type:    New Feature
Assignee:   Unassigned
Components:   DataFrame
Created:   07/Feb/15 1:14 PM
Priority:    Major
Reporter:   Dan Putler <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=dputler>

Currently Mllib modeling tools work only with double data. However, data tables in practice often have a set of categorical fields (factors in R), that need to be converted to a set of 0/1 indicator variables (making the data actually used in a modeling algorithm completely numeric). In R, this is handled in modeling functions using the model.matrix function. Similar functionality needs to be available within Spark.

The WIP branch I have is at https://github.com/shivaram/sparkr-pkg/tree/sparkr-runner – I have so far tested this locally with a Standalone Spark master and with a local YARN cluster (in a Cloudera VM).

I'd like to test this in a multi-machine YARN cluster and it would be great if you could help with that. Let me know if you want to try it and I can give some build / test instructions if necessary.

Felix Cheung <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=felixcheung> The best way to try this would be be to clone my github branch and build from source (instead of using install_github). This is mainly because I haven't packaged the `sparkR-submit` script as a part of the installed package. So the instructions to install this would be something like
git clone https://github.com/shivaram/SparkR-pkg.git -b sparkr-runner SparkR-pkg-runner-test
cd SparkR-pkg-runner-test
USE_YARN=1 SPARK_YARN_VERSION=2.4.0 SPARK_HADOOP_VERSION=2.4.0 R CMD INSTALL pkg/

You will then need to repeat this on all the nodes or copy out the installed lib directory to all the nodes in the cluster – Longer term we probably try to send a tar/gz via YARN and automatically install it on the worker nodes, but I haven't figured that out yet.

Following that you can try out something like
export SPARK_HOME=<your_spark_install_dir>
export /YARN_CONF_DIR=<dir_where_yarn_configs_are>
./sparkR-submit --master yarn-client ./examples/pi.R yarn-client 4

Let me know if something needs more clarification.

And you are right – the last part about SparkConf is SPARKR-141 <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-141>

messages.subject: [JIRA] (SPARKR-184) Support JdbcRDD
messages.subject_clean: [JIRA] (SPARKR-184) Support JdbcRDD
messages.body_plain:
Shivaram Venkataraman <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=shivaram> commented on  SPARKR-184 <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-184>

Re: Support JdbcRDD <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-184>

As far as I can see we don't need to use RJDBC. I think Martin Tapp <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=doctapp> was giving an example of the user-facing API that we can support.
The work we need to do is just take these string descriptions (for JDBC classname, classPath, databaseName etc.) and create JDBC connections inside the JVM using a wrapper class. The JDBC test suite has an example of how we can do this https://github.com/apache/spark/blob/master/sql/core/src/test/scala/org/apache/spark/sql/jdbc/JDBCSuite.scala#L34

However I am not sure we explicitly need to work on this – Given that we are working towards the DataFrame API, it should be possible to add JDBC backends to that and so we may get this for free.

SparkR <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR> /  <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-198> SPARKR-198 <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-198>
Add a health check from SparkR backend to R process <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-198>
Issue Type:    Improvement
Assignee:   Unassigned
Components:   R JVM Bridge
Created:   11/Feb/15 8:38 AM
Environment:

This is related to  <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-185>
SPARKR-185  and is intended to ensure that the backend always exits when the R process exits.

The proposed solution is to open a server socket on the R side and then have the Java process send periodic heart-beats to this socket.

Note: We don't need this for the spark-submit case because the JVM comes up first there and exits when the child R process exits.
Priority:    Major
Reporter:   Shivaram Venkataraman <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=shivaram>

messages.subject: [JIRA] (SPARKR-153) Support fold, aggregate (similar to reduce, reduceByKey)
messages.subject_clean: [JIRA] (SPARKR-153) Support fold, aggregate (similar to reduce, reduceByKey)
messages.body_plain:
Sun Rui <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=sunrui> commented on  SPARKR-153 <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-153>

Re: Support fold, aggregate (similar to reduce, reduceByKey) <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-153>

I looked at the implementation of fold() in Spark and pySpark. I am confused that there seems a bug in them: fold() function is applied to each partition with zeroValue. This makes the result of fold() may depend on the partition number. for example, in pySpark,
>>> sc.parallelize([1, 2, 3, 4, 5]).fold(1, operator.add)
28
>>> sc.parallelize([1, 2, 3, 4, 5],3).fold(1, operator.add)
19
>>> sc.parallelize([1, 2, 3, 4, 5],4).fold(1, operator.add)
20
>>> sc.parallelize([1, 2, 3, 4, 5],5).fold(1, operator.add)
21
Is this an expected behavior?

I think the proper implemenation would be apply fold() function in each partition without zeroValue, and fold the results of each partition with zeroValue.

Do you have any comments?

messages.body_plain:
Shivaram Venkataraman <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=shivaram> commented on  SPARKR-141 <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-141>

Re: Read spark-defaults.conf in SparkR startup <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-141>

I looked at this recently and I think the existing arguments to `sparkR.init` pretty much cover all the options that are exposed in SparkConf.

We could split things out of the function arguments into a separate SparkConf object (something like PySpark https://github.com/apache/spark/blob/master/python/pyspark/conf.py) but the setter-methods don't translate very well to the style we use in SparkR. For example it would be something like setAppName(setMaster(conf, "local"), "SparkR") instead of conf.setMaster().setAppName()

The other thing brought up by this JIRA is that we should parse arguments passed to spark-submit or set in spark-defaults.conf. I think this should automatically happen with SPARKR-178 <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-178>

Sun Rui <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=sunrui> Zongheng Yang <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=concretevitamin> Any thoughts on this ?

Felix Cheung <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=felixcheung> commented on  SPARKR-178 <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-178>

Re: Create a R runner to integrate with Spark Submit <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-178>

I've tested this against CDH 5.3 cluster in YARN mode.

I installed from my branch as such:
```
USE_YARN=1 SPARK_VERSION=1.1.0 SPARK_YARN_VERSION=2.5.0-cdh5.3.0 SPARK_HADOOP_VERSION=2.5.0-cdh5.3.0 R
```
```R
library(devtools)
install_github("felixcheung/SparkR-pkg", ref="working", subdir="pkg")
```

And then ran sparkR-submit as such:
```
export YARN_CONF_DIR=/etc/hadoop/conf
export SPARK_HOME=/opt/cloudera/parcels/CDH-5.3.0-1.cdh5.3.0.p0.30/lib/spark
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/java/jdk1.7.0_67-cloudera
/usr/lib64/R/library/SparkR/sparkR-submit --master yarn-client ./pi.R yarn-client 4
```

I made 2 small changes to make this work:
https://github.com/felixcheung/SparkR-pkg/commit/e3079e4b562ac3a91aa6c76ec098b70c3934578d
https://github.com/felixcheung/SparkR-pkg/commit/614da5d9b0f6e19b7d8476506117ffcd6e7685aa

messages.subject_clean: [JIRA] (SPARKR-202) Default AMI Needs Updating, EC2 Scripts Fail
messages.body_plain:
Amos <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=elbamos> created an issue

SparkR <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR> /  <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-202> SPARKR-202 <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-202>
Default AMI Needs Updating, EC2 Scripts Fail <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-202>
Issue Type:    Bug
Assignee:   Unassigned
Components:   Deployment
Created:   17/Feb/15 12:53 PM
Environment:

Amazon EC2
Priority:    Major
Reporter:   Amos <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=elbamos>

The current Amazon EC2 script is dysfunctional, and the AMI is seriously outdated. A few issues:
The EC2 security profile needs to open port 7077 on the master.
R on the AMI is at version 3.1.1, and was installed without a BLAS lib. Besides the speed issue (people should at least have the option of switching to an optimized BLAS), some packages, such as `slam`, simply won't compile unless R is built with a shared BLAS library.

Then there's this: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/27039954/intermittent-timeout-exception-using-spark, and some other similar questions on stackoverflow, where the solution seems to require disabling the firewall completely.

(I still can't get this problem to go away, even after disabling the firewall!)

But either way, with the version of R on the ami, its in serious need of an update.

messages.body_plain:
Shivaram Venkataraman <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=shivaram> created an issue

SparkR <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR> /  <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-204> SPARKR-204 <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-204>
Use random port for SparkR Backend <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-204>
Issue Type:    New Feature
Assignee:   Unassigned
Components:   R JVM Bridge
Created:   18/Feb/15 6:23 PM
Priority:    Major
Reporter:   Shivaram Venkataraman <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=shivaram>

Right now we use a fixed port (12345) by default for the backend. This can create collisions when multiple backends are used on the same machine. We should use a pattern similar to Spark, Py4J where we start at a known port and then incrementally try to find an open port

cc Felix Cheung <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=felixcheung>

Zongheng Yang <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=concretevitamin> commented on  SPARKR-141 <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-141>

Re: Read spark-defaults.conf in SparkR startup <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-141>

IMO using a named list provides more flexibility: it's ordinary data that users can operate/transform on. Using only parameter-passing in the constructor locks users in operating on code instead of data. It'd also be easier to just return the saved named list if we're going to implement getConf()?

Some relevant discussions: https://aphyr.com/posts/321-builders-vs-option-maps

Issue Type:    Bug

Environment:

AWS, sequenceiq/docker-spark, SparkR

Reporter:   XW Gong <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=xgong>

I have a AWS instance and am running the sequenceiq/docker-spark (including hadoop and spark) on it. The R and SparkR were installed on AWS.

After I initiated a spark context using the following command:
sc <- sparkR.init(master='spark://ip-10-64-65-168:7077', appName="ER")

The connect was built successfully. But the error messages popped up soon. The main line of the message is: "ERROR TaskSchedulerImpl: Lost an executor 0 (already removed): remote Akka client disassociated". And the same error messages will repeat for executor 1, 2, ....

I am new to spark, and I have done online research for a few weeks, but still could not fix it. Any ideas or hints will be appreciated very much! Thanks!!!

Hi,

I know this is an issue that others have faced a number of times, but none of the posted solutions have worked for me. I am unable to build SparkR behind my proxy with either sbt or maven. I have tried building it in R from github using the devtools library, and have also tried cloning the github repository and building outside of R. I have also tried building it with the USE_MAVEN=1 option. I have installed sbt v0.13.6 via yum and it appears to be running correctly (with SBT_OPTS and JAVA_OPTS set to include my http and https proxy settings and authentication details, and also with http_proxy and https_proxy settings set). I have also modified the build.sbt file to reflect my specific versions of Spark, Hadoop and Scala.

Sean Farrell <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=safarrell> Are you able to build any other maven projects using your proxy settings on the same machine ? I just want to figure out if this is a maven-level configuration issue or if this is something specific to SparkR.

BTW The R CMD INSTALL just ends up invoking mvn under the covers, so you could try to debug the `mvn` invocation directly by doing something like
cd pkg/src
mvn -Dhadoop.version=1.0.4 -Dspark.version=1.2.0 -DskipTests clean package shade:shade

If the above command fails similarly you can debug further using any extra maven flags or other online pointers like http://stackoverflow.com/questions/1251192/how-do-i-use-maven-through-a-proxy

If the mvn command works but running `install-dev.sh` doesn't work then its a bug in the script that we'll need to fix.

messages.subject_clean: [JIRA] (SPARKR-205) SparkR does not work right after sparkR.init(). Keeps reporting Error "Lost an executor"
messages.body_plain:
XW Gong <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=xgong> commented on  SPARKR-205 <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-205>

Re: SparkR does not work right after sparkR.init(). Keeps reporting Error "Lost an executor" <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-205>

Hi Shivaram,

Thanks for your quick tips. It seems that the error was fixed. (Please go to the bottom for my new questions, thanks!)

Here are what I did:
In the first trial, I downloaded the SparkR-pkg from Github, and run the following command:
SPARK_VERSION=1.2.0 ./install-dev.sh
Then I found that the SparkR package was installed into the /lib directory of SparkR-pkg, NOT into the R library directory. I was not sure if I could copy it to the R library directory directly. So I tried the other way.

In the 2nd trial, I edited the build.sbt file under /pkg/src/, changed the value of defaultSparkVersion to 1.2.0. Then I used "R CMD build" to create a R source package file SparkR_0.1.tar.gz. Then in the R shell, I installed the SparkR from the source package file.

After that, I can ran the sparkcontext instantiation line without the "lost executors" errors.

**************************************New question****************************************
1) I created the SparkContext using the following command:
sc <- sparkR.init(master='spark://ip-10-64-65-168:7077',appName='ER_test',sparkEnvir=list(spark.executor.memory='10g',spark.num.executors='4',spark.executor.cores='1'))

I expected to see 4 executors. But on the slave webUI, I always see only ONE executor 0, even when I submitted some testing example, such as wordcount.

Any idea?

2) When I ran the wordcount example, I got the similar error message as in the post-173 (https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-173). I followed your comment in the post to change the hadoop version.

What I did is similar to the above. That is, edited build.sbt and changed the defaultHadoopVersion to 2.6.0. Then rebuilt the SparkR package.

After that, when I instantiated sparkContext, I got a WARN message: "NativeCodeLoader: Unable to load native-hadoop library for your platform... using builtin-java classes where applicable."

Is it OK?

Thanks again for your kind and generous help!!!!!!

messages.subject_clean: [JIRA] (SPARKR-208) SQLContext.parquetFile wrong arguments
messages.body_plain:
Evert Lammerts <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=evertlammerts> created an issue

SparkR <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR> /  <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-208> SPARKR-208 <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-208>
SQLContext.parquetFile wrong arguments <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-208>
Issue Type:    Bug
Assignee:   Unassigned
Components:   DataFrame
Created:   25/Feb/15 5:47 AM
Environment:

SparkR sparkr-sql branch + HDP 2.2 (Hadoop / YARN 2.6.0) + Spark 1.3.0 master + R 3.1.2 on RHEL Server 6.6
Priority:    Major
Reporter:   Evert Lammerts <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=evertlammerts>

calling parquetFile (in the sparkr-sql branch) fails with:

> parquetFile(sqlCtx, path)
parquetFile on 2 failed with java.util.NoSuchElementException: next on empty iterator
java.util.NoSuchElementException: next on empty iterator
        at scala.collection.Iterator$$anon$2.next(Iterator.scala:39)
        at scala.collection.Iterator$$anon$2.next(Iterator.scala:37)
        at scala.collection.IndexedSeqLike$Elements.next(IndexedSeqLike.scala:64)
        at scala.collection.IterableLike$class.head(IterableLike.scala:91)
        at scala.collection.mutable.ArrayOps$ofRef.scala$collection$IndexedSeqOptimized$$super$head(ArrayOps.scala:108)
        at scala.collection.IndexedSeqOptimized$class.head(IndexedSeqOptimized.scala:120)
        at scala.collection.mutable.ArrayOps$ofRef.head(ArrayOps.scala:108)
        at edu.berkeley.cs.amplab.sparkr.SparkRBackendHandler.handleMethodCall(SparkRBackendHandler.scala:111)
        at edu.berkeley.cs.amplab.sparkr.SparkRBackendHandler.channelRead0(SparkRBackendHandler.scala:60)
        at edu.berkeley.cs.amplab.sparkr.SparkRBackendHandler.channelRead0(SparkRBackendHandler.scala:22)

This is caused by edu.berkeley.cs.amplab.sparkr.SparkRBackendHandler#matchMethod. It tries to find a method with signature org.apache.spark.sql.SQLContext.parquetFile(java.lang.String), but only org.apache.spark.sql.SQLContext.parquetFile(java.lang.String...) exists (varargs argument).

There are three ways of fixing this:
change the parquetFile signature in SQLContext.R
change edu.berkeley.cs.amplab.sparkr.SparkRBackendHandler#matchMethod to handle matching of varargs arguments
change org.apache.spark.sql.SQLContext.parquetFile signature to a single String

There's something to say for option 3, because jsonFiledoesn't have a varargs signature either. It's a breaking change though.

Option 2 should be done anyway, I guess. I believe this is the most simple solution, but I'm not sure how to go about it. Maybe check both for signatures of type T and type T[]. Any ideas?

For an easy fix, option 1 is most suitable. I'll put in a pull request of code that I've tested and that works for me.

Issue Type:    Bug
Assignee:   Unassigned
Created:   25/Feb/15 5:18 PM
Environment:

RHEL6.5 running on an AWS EC2 cluster with Spark and Hadoop deployed via CDH 5.3.1.
Priority:    Major
Reporter:   Sean Farrell <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=safarrell>

I've managed to build and deploy SparkR on our cluster (through yarn), and I think it is setup correctly. However, when I run the pi.R or wordcount.R example scripts I get the following errors:

java.lang.reflect.InvocationTargetException
...
Caused by: java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: com.google.common.hash.HashFunction.hashInt(I)Lcom/google/common/hash/HashCode;

When running the pi.R script it appears to still complete successfully, but the wordcount.R script fails (see below for complete error output). This error appears to crop up due to Guava incompatibility issues with Spark and Hive, but I don't know why this would be causing the wordcount script to fail.

For reference, here are the environment variables I have set:
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/java/jdk1.7.0_67-cloudera
export SCALA_HOME=/usr/local/share/scala-2.11.5
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/cloudera/parcels/CDH-5.3.1-1.cdh5.3.1.p0.5/lib/hadoop-0.20-mapreduce/lib/native/Linux-amd64-64
export YARN_CONF_DIR=/etc/hadoop/conf.cloudera.yarn

I am invoking the wordcount.R script as follows:
Rscript wordcount.R yarn-client hdfs://user/sean.farrell/temp.txt

Where temp.txt is a text file located in my hdfs directory. I've also tried running it line by line in R and it crashes when it tries to read the text file into an RDD, i.e. at this line:
lines <- textFile(sc, "hdfs://user/sean.farrell/temp.txt")

Is this an indication that my configuration is not setup correctly?

Launch R worker by a daemon <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/browse/SPARKR-214>
Issue Type:    Improvement
Assignee:   Davies <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=davies>
Created:   26/Feb/15 12:04 PM
Priority:    Critical
Reporter:   Davies <https://sparkr.atlassian.net/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=davies>

The Spark executor could use lots of memory to cache some data, then it's very expensive to fork a R process (or easy to fail).

The solution is fork a lightweight daemon (in R) process in the beginning (when needed), call the daemon to launch R worker when needed.

This is only works in Linux/Mac, In Windows, it will still fork a R worker from JVM.

FWIW I also found that the SBT resolver somehow ends up picking the guava 14 dependency and hence I wasn't seeing these errors while building with SBT and Spark 1.2.1. I don't know why this difference exists, but thats a different issue I guess.
--- a/pkg/src/pom.xml
+++ b/pkg/src/pom.xml
@@ -109,6 +109,11 @@
       </exclusions>
     </dependency>
     <dependency>
+      <groupId>com.google.guava</groupId>
+      <artifactId>guava</artifactId>
+      <version>14.0.1</version>
+    </dependency>
+    <dependency>
       <groupId>org.slf4j</groupId>
       <artifactId>slf4j-log4j12</artifactId>
       <version>1.7.2</version>

Hi Shivaram,

that fixed it, thanks! I'm now able to run the wordcount script without any errors, so I think the guava issue was what was causing it to crash before (though I don't know why). It doesn't appear to cause any issues with YARN, though I'll keep you posted if anything crops up. I don't know how Hive works around the guava dependency issues, and I'm still not sure whether that had anything to do with our issue anyway (I came across a post that reported a similar error message that mentioned a Hive/Spark incompatibility issue regarding Guava: http://mail-archives.us.apache.org/mod_mbox/spark-user/201410.mbox/%3CCAAswR-5Jum=FLFrrWr_BFYO6+jiM0i...@mail.gmail.com%3E <http://mail-archives.us.apache.org/mod_mbox/spark-user/201410.mbox/%3CCAAswR-5Jum=FLF...@mail.gmail.com%3E>).

Unfortunately I wasn't able to build SparkR with SBT as it didn't seem to be able to authenticate through our proxy.

Thanks again, I think this ticket can be closed now.

Cheers,

Sean
